title: Responsibility
hookLine: carrying your share, and a bit more

lines: I WILL BE SURETY FOR HIM.
cards: Famine, and the grain from Egypt is running out. The brothers have to go back down, and the ruler in Egypt has told them: don't come back without your youngest brother. Their father Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go.
He has already lost one son. Reuben tries first, with an offer no father could accept. Then Judah steps forward: "I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him."
Jacob lets them go. Today's word is what Judah just put on his own back.

teach.b: Achrayut. Responsibility. Turn it four ways.
Judah doesn't say I'll try, or I'll keep an eye on him. He says: require him of my hand. That's the heart of the trait: not doing everything, but being the one who answers for something.
Second, the test. In Egypt, a silver cup is found in Benjamin's sack, and the ruler says Benjamin will stay behind as a slave. The others could go home free.
Judah steps forward again and asks to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place. His promise gets checked, and it holds. Third, the old question.
Much earlier in Genesis, Cain is asked where his brother is, and answers with a question: am I my brother's keeper? God doesn't answer yes or no. He asks back: what hast thou done?
Long after, Judah answers Cain's question with his body. Fourth, the share.
Pirkei Avot keeps a saying of Rabbi Tarfon: it is not on you to finish the work, and you are not free to walk away from it. Not carrying the whole world, which would crush anyone.
Carrying your share, and a bit more, and not setting it down when it gets heavy. Yesterday's honor treated others as weighty. Responsibility lets some of that weight rest on you.

how: Mussar students work on achrayut by choosing one area where they will be the person who answers, and Jewish teaching often pairs Judah's surety for Benjamin with Rabbi Tarfon's saying in Pirkei Avot.

o: guilt you feel after something goes wrong
responsibility: being the one who answers for it
a duty to fix every problem by yourself

p: I will be surety for him
the silver cup in his sack

s: Rabbi Tarfon says you must finish the whole work yourself
he says it is not on you to finish it, and you are not free to walk away from it.
in Egypt, Judah offers to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place
the promise he made to his father gets tested, and he keeps it.
God answers Cain's question with a plain yes
God answers with another question: what hast thou done? Judah's story answers it later.

games.q: you're Judah. the silver cup is in Benjamin's sack, and the ruler says Benjamin stays as a slave. the rest of you can go home. what do you do?
o: go home and tell your father what happened.
offer to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place.
games.why: Judah steps forward and asks to stay in Benjamin's place. he had told his father: "of my hand shalt thou require him."

practice: Look for something sitting between people, where everyone assumes someone else will handle it: a family call nobody makes, a problem at work that keeps getting forwarded, a promise that was half yours.
Pick one and say quietly, the way Judah did, this one is mine, then decide your first step and when: just your share and a bit more. If you pray, you can name it in your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Achrayut. Responsibility: becoming the one who answers for something, the way Judah answered for Benjamin. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: carry your share. You're not asked to finish it, only not to walk away. See you on the next step.
